## 56cfec365918

**Classification: reproduced distribution shortcut / missing default-domain witness.** The validator accepts two disconnected 2×2 components with the same color. On `checks/audit/56cfec365918/input.json`, the canonical Racket authority (`executed_rule_hash=5e86ac335c4b`) treats components independently and keeps a diagonal in each, producing four colored cells. A plausible global-color shortcut keeps only the first and last cells of the color class and produces two cells; see `racket.json` versus `rival.json`.

The counterexample is validator-lawful (`validator_findings=[]`), but a default scan of seeds 0–19 and sample indices 0–9 at medium difficulty found 0/200 draws with repeated-color multiple components. Thus the generated distribution does not teach component identity independently of color identity. Exact hashes, scan range, command, and paths are in `checks/audit/56cfec365918/witness.json`. I made no changes to this audit-only target.

## 56cfec365918

**Classification: reproduced canonical-fitting shortcut / missing generated witness.** No audit-target files were changed.

Generator SHA-256 `280da1a61c35d7a6f81619e93fc884e12f267bd8de247e4d03160cf28e5e060e`; executed/catalog rule hash `5e86ac335c4b`.

A plausible rival treats every nonzero color as one global object and retains only that color's lexicographically first and last cells. With one uniquely colored 2×2 block per color, it is indistinguishable from the intended per-block main diagonal. It fits **4/4 canonical pairs** and **32/32 fresh medium generated cases** (seeds 0–7, sample indices 0–3; 32 unique inputs; all validator-clean). The scan found **0/32** inputs with two disconnected components of the same color.

The validator accepts two disconnected color-4 2×2 blocks. Racket authority keeps the main diagonal of each block—four cells—whereas the global-color rival keeps only the first cell of the first block and last cell of the second. This discriminator belongs to the validator's documented grammar but is unreachable under the default unique-color sampler.

Evidence: `checks/audit/56cfec365918/comparison.json`, `input.json`, `racket.json`, and the 32-case `generated_racket.json`.

triage.reason: Accepted source-bound findings-only audits; exact reproductions retained. Generator contract/teaching defects are repair candidates, no-issue outcomes remain bounded; duplicates do not count as new defects.

## 56cfec365918

**Classification: reproduced shortcut / missing generated witness.**  
Target generator SHA-256: `280da1a61c35d7a6f81619e93fc884e12f267bd8de247e4d03160cf28e5e060e`.  
Rule hash: `5e86ac335c4b`.

The canonical demonstrations use each foreground color in exactly one 2×2 block. A plausible shortcut is: **for each nonzero color, keep only its lexicographically first and last cell**. On one 2×2 block, that produces the same diagonal pair as the intended per-object rule, so it fits the demonstrated structure.

I constructed an 8×8 input with two disconnected 2×2 blocks of color 4: one at rows 1–2 / columns 1–2 and one at rows 5–6 / columns 5–6. The target validator accepts it. The actual Racket rule keeps two diagonal cells from **each** component—four cells total. The rival keeps only the first and last cell over the whole color—two cells total—so it disagrees.

A scan of seeds 0–19 and sample indices 0–9 at medium difficulty found **0/200** default generated inputs with two disconnected components of the same nonzero color. Therefore the hand-constructed input belongs to the validator's documented domain, but the default distribution does not teach this distinction in the scanned census.

Exact input, outputs, hashes, validator result, scan denominator, and reproduction command: `checks/audit-56cfec365918-counterexample.json`.

triage.reason: Both audit reports retained against exact target hashes; census results remain reviewer-reported. Repair targets are not modified by audits. Findings are visible to future assignments via task indexes.

## 56cfec365918

**Finding type: validator-accepted but unreachable discriminator.** Generator SHA-256 `280da1a61c35d7a6f81619e93fc884e12f267bd8de247e4d03160cf28e5e060e`; executed rule hash `5e86ac335c4b`.

Every canonical and generated 2×2 block receives a distinct color. Therefore the shortcut “treat all cells of each color as one global object and retain only the global bounding-box top-left and bottom-right” fits all 4 canonical pairs and 100 generated probes.

Exact discriminator—two separated 2×2 blocks of the same color:

```json
[[0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0],
 [0,4,4,0,0,4,4,0],
 [0,4,4,0,0,4,4,0],
 [0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]]
```

The supported Racket rule transforms each connected block independently:

```json
[[0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0],
 [0,4,0,0,0,4,0,0],
 [0,0,4,0,0,0,4,0],
 [0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0]]
```

The shortcut retains only `(1,1)` and `(2,6)`. This discriminator **passes `self_check`**, so it belongs to the validator's documented grammar, but ordinary generation cannot emit it because every block receives a unique color. Exact grids, outputs, hashes, command, and cwd are in `checks/audit/56cfec365918/witness.json` and `racket.json`.

No fix was applied.
